lines: Avery Brooks
+1 (555) 010-3319 | avery.brooks@example.com | example.com/in/abrooks
Date of birth: 9 Jan 1998 | Nationality: Brazilian
EDUCATION
Eastmoor University | B.S. in Statistics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Pinecrest Insurance | Junior Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2020 - Jul 2022
- Ran the checkout A/B test until significance by checking the p-value every day and stopping on the first day it fell below 0.05.
- Analyzed 18 months of call-center data; my findings moved two agents to the evening peak and cut average hold time from 9 to 5 minutes.
- Writes the team's SQL style guide and review checklist, which cut query errors found in review by half.

- Automated the monthly fraud-flag extract while also maintaining the team calendar, answering ad hoc questions from sales, updating onboarding documents and covering the help desk on Fridays, which saved the fraud team 10 hours a month.
Brightcart Retail | Data Analyst | Metro City, USA | Aug 2022 - Jun 2025
- Built the weekly retention dashboard for 2.4M customers that marketing used to retarget lapsed buyers, lifting 90-day repeat purchase from 22% to 27%.
- Cut the monthly revenue report from 3 days of spreadsheet work to 2 hours by moving it to scheduled SQL queries and a shared dashboard.
- Found customers with no orders by left-joining the orders table to the customers table and counting rows with a null customer name.

- Joining 40 source tables, deduplicating customer records across two loyalty systems and rebuilding the attribution logic in dbt-style SQL models, raised the share of orders tied to a campaign from 58% to 81%.
- Presented the quarterly customer review to the leadership team, and two of its three recommendations were funded in the next budget.
- Trained 20 merchandisers to answer their own questions with the self-serve dashboards, halving ad hoc data requests.
PROJECTS
City Bike-Share Demand Study | Independent Project | Python, SQL | Jan 2025 - Present
- Modeled hourly bike-share demand for 120 stations from 2 years of public trip data, forecasting next-day demand within 12% mean absolute error.
- Cut empty-station hours from 300 to 200 a week, a 50% reduction, in a replay of last summer's rebalancing.
- Raised forecast hit rate by 15% across 120 stations, from 60% to 75%, by adding weather and event features.
Food Pantry Visit Analysis | Volunteer, Team of 3 | Excel, SQL | Mar 2023 - Aug 2023
- Mapped 14 months of pantry visits by hour and day, so the pantry moved one volunteer shift and cut the Saturday line from 50 to 20 minutes.
- Cleaned 9,000 handwritten visit logs into a single table and matched repeat visitors, giving the pantry its first count of unique households.
- Wrote a one-page guide the pantry coordinator used to update the visit table each month after the project ended.
SKILLS
Tools: SQL, Python, Excel
Methods: dashboards, forecasting, metric design, data-quality checks

items.says: Confirm the profile link works and leads to a current profile.
Add a portfolio or project link if it shows relevant work.
Remove the date of birth and nationality for most U.S. applications.
items.because: They are generally unnecessary and can introduce bias.

items.says: Add relevant academic detail only if it strengthens your candidacy.
Put Brightcart before Pinecrest.
items.because: Employers should see your most recent experience first.

items.says: Do not present daily p-value checking and stopping below 0.05 as sound experimental practice.
items.because: That stopping rule can inflate false positives.

items.says: Clarify whether the staffing change followed your recommendation.
Clarify whether the hold-time reduction was measured after the change.
Change “Writes” to past tense.
Explain how the reduction in review errors was measured.
Separate the fraud automation from the other duties.
items.because: The long list obscures what produced the 10-hour monthly saving.

items.says: Avoid attributing the entire repeat-purchase increase to the dashboard without evidence isolating its effect.
Clarify whether “3 days to 2 hours” compares elapsed turnaround time or hands-on work.
A null customer name in this left join does not establish that a customer has no orders.
items.because: The missing match should be identified using an appropriate field from the orders table.

items.says: Explain the business value of the analysis, not just the join operation.
Fix the grammar around “Joining …, raised.”
Make the relationship between the modeling changes and the 58%-to-81% increase easier to follow.
Add what the funded recommendations accomplished, if known.
items.because: That outcome would be more informative than funding alone.

items.says: Specify the period used to compare ad hoc request volume, if available.
“12% mean absolute error” uses an ambiguous metric label.
items.because: Mean absolute error normally has the units of demand.

items.says: Name the percentage-based metric used and, if useful, the forecast horizon and evaluation period.
The drop from 300 to 200 is a 33% reduction, not 50%.
Clearly label the empty-station result as a simulated replay.
items.because: It was not an observed operational result.

items.says: Define what counted as a forecast “hit.”
The rise from 60% to 75% is not an unqualified 15% increase.
items.because: It is 15 percentage points, or a 25% relative increase.

items.says: Clarify how the Saturday wait-time change was measured.
Clarify whether other changes contributed to the wait-time reduction.
Describe the 9,000 logs as individual entries if they were not separate documents.
Add specific tools or platforms used in the experience bullets if you can discuss them confidently.
items.because: The current skills list undersells the work shown above.

Be ready to account for the period since the June 2025 role ended.
